# Pre-registration: HAT-P-32 b, MicroObservatory night of 2026-09-21 UT

Judgment lines written 2026-09-22 09:0x UTC by Opus (running on claude-opus-5; Fable
credits exhausted until 09-24). Committed before the fit; the fit's start time is in
wasp-style run log `hatp32_0921_run.log`.

Frames: 104, 03:54 to 09:04 UT, 60.0 s Clear.
Archive (NEA pscomppars, fetched 2026-09-21 18:13 UTC): P 2.15000820 +/- 1.3e-07 d,
T0 2455867.402743 +/- 4.9e-05, T14 3.120 h, Rp/Rs 0.1489 (depth 2.22%), a/Rs 5.344,
inc 88.98, e 0.159, Teff 6001.0, V 11.439. Epoch 2529: predicted Tmid 2461304.77348 (06:33 UT),
ingress 05:00, egress 08:07; 66 min pre-ingress and 57 min post-egress in the window
(full). Propagated ephemeris bar 0.5 min.

Predictions:
- Sky judged by stars per frame and the target's aperture flux (night_triage), not the background.
  If the counts hold through 05:00-08:07 and the seed target is >200 ADU above background:
  QC PASS. I am predicting which, because there is a reason: every one of the 104 frames graded
  clear, 63 of them in transit with both ingress and egress covered, the depth is 2.22% against a
  predicted 0.83% scatter (scatter/depth 0.38, the most favourable ratio of any night I have opened),
  and the archive geometry is a near-central transit (a/Rs 5.344, inc 88.98 gives b = 0.095), so the
  grazing-solution failure mode has a long way to travel to reach b = 1. If this night comes back
  MARGINAL the cause is mechanical, not atmospheric, and the first place to look is the one named below.
- Scatter, from the V-magnitude calibration (0.84% at V 11.57 on 2026-09-05, +0.05%/mag from three clean nights, revised 2026-09-18):
  ~0.83%. On a 2.22% depth that is scatter/depth 0.38; with 0.425 giving
  8.2 min at ~3 min cadence, expected Tmid bar ~7 min (range 5-11; two clean nights gave 9.6 and 8.6 against 6.7 and 9.0 predicted, so the bar model is two-point-crude).
  Under 4 min: calibration wrong the other way. Over 13 min: worse night than the counts show.
- Tmid within 1 sigma (that bar) of 2461304.77348. WHAT A MISS WOULD AND WOULD NOT MEAN, and this is
  the part the WASP-52 b week rewrote: with a propagated archive bar of 0.5 min against an expected
  measurement bar of ~7 min, MY bar dominates by a factor of fourteen. So an offset here cannot be
  blamed on a stale prior the way row 43's +13 min was half-explained by one. If |O-C| lands beyond
  ~7 min I check three things in this order before believing the planet: (1) the coverage of the
  comparison star the transit fit actually used -- this is the mechanism that produced +7 min on
  WASP-52 b out of nothing but lost frames, and post_run_check now prints and warns on it; (2)
  ExoClock's own ephemeris for this target, because "the archive bar is small" is exactly what I
  believed before ExoClock showed it 6.2 min stale, and a small formal bar is not the same claim as
  an unstale one; (3) an independent refit of the same detrended points. Only if all three survive is
  the offset a statement about HAT-P-32 b, and even then one night is not a statement.
- THE NAMED RISK, stated fresh because it was learned two days ago: EXOTIC's comparison selector can
  prefer a star whose PSF-quality filter drops a tenth of the frames over a full-coverage star a few
  hundredths of a percent worse on suitability. On WASP-52 b that cost 7 of 70 points, concentrated
  in the first half of the transit, and turned a passing night into a grazing fit 7 minutes late. The
  six comparisons here are 3.06x to 5.50x the target and all sit in the drift box; the prediction is
  that the selected one keeps at least 94 of 104 frames. If it does not, I refit with it excluded
  before any number reaches the ledger, and I say so in the row rather than quoting the first fit.
- Caveat I cannot test tonight: the archive row carries e = 0.159 for this planet, which is contested
  and which EXOTIC's model does not use (it fits a circular orbit). If the duration comes back
  materially short or long of 3.12 h with a central b, that is a candidate explanation and not a
  fault in the night.
- Depth within 1 sigma of 2.22%; Rp/Rs within 1 sigma of 0.1489.
- If stars-per-frame falls by more than half at any point between 05:00 and 08:07, or the target is under
  ~200 ADU above background in the seed frame: expect FAIL or a rejected night, and the record will say so
  with no depth or timing claim.
- Any printed bar under 0.001 d is a replaced bar (#1401) and gets refit before the ledger.
- First-frame coordinates from a local plate solve; drift by star-pair voting; comps in the triage box within a
  brightness factor of the target; #1409 confirms the rest.
- Not submitted regardless; checkpoint holds.

parameters.Fit parameter point estimate: Best-fit likelihood point; uncertainties are posterior spread.
parameters.Pre-UltraNest LM boundary scout note: LM solution and covariance envelope were interior after 4 iteration(s).
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline parameter-fit no: Used a0 and a2 from the previous fast UltraNest fit for the full-resolution final run.
parameters.Out-of-transit baseline detrending note: only 8 pre-ingress and 19 post-egress out-of-transit point(s) were available; need more than 12 on each side to fit a linear baseline.
parameters.Sparse posterior live-point extension no: Applied full-resolution selected comparison-star final UltraNest run (200->1200 minimum live points) with fixed a0/a2 from the previous fast UltraNest fit.
parameters.Final residual rejection note: No residual outliers exceeded 3.0 sigma from the iterated median residual (-0.0790%, stdev=0.6983%).
parameters.Uncertainty interpretation note: The primary Rp/R* and radius-ratio area-depth uncertainties use model+red-noise when available. The red-noise uncertainty inflates the data-fit standard error by a residual time-binning beta factor before combining it with the model posterior. The flux baseline red-noise uncertainty is the out-of-transit baseline component used for the final-plot baseline band; the transit-depth red-noise uncertainty already includes both the in-transit and baseline terms. The same residual time-binning beta factor is applied to the posterior uncertainties for Tmid, a/Rs, inclination, and impact parameter when reporting their primary model+red-noise uncertainties. The flux-scatter equivalent is also shown as a diagnostic of the full residual scatter around the model.
